An amazing accomplishment worth spotlighting.

Congrats to @DavidMoss @OwenSparks and @scotsrule08!


Spencer (@scotsrule08)

NYC to LA Cannonball with Tesla FSD is done!

@DavidMoss, @OwenSparks, and I are proud to announce that we have broken the record for the fastest fully autonomous drive from New York City to Los Angeles!

We left the Red Ball Garage in New York, NY 47 hours, 15 minutes, and 39 seconds ago, and now have ended in Redondo Beach, CA at the Portofino Hotel

(2,886 miles / 4,645 km)

This was accomplished with Tesla FSD v14.3.6, beating the previous record of 49:55:57 by 2 hours, 40 minutes, and 18 seconds, with absolutely zero disengagements.

Huge thanks to @AlexRoy144 for years of inspiration. Thank you to all of the teams at @Tesla, with particular shout-outs to @Tesla_AI and @TeslaCharging for their phenomenal efforts. This would not have been possible without them.

This update came out hours ago, but our backend failed to post the update here because Mapbox did not have geographical data for the initial vehicle.

This is a first time occurrence, so we've patched this portion of the code to continue with posting if a location can't be found.

The following feature is included: Rear Display

Disable rear touchscreen controls from the center display by going to App Launcher > Rear > Lock Rear Display. Content selected from the center display will continue to play in the rear.

The following feature is included: Set Arrival Energy

Set your desired Arrival Energy for any trip from your phone. Open the location tab in the Tesla Mobile App, enter your destination, and tap Set Arrival Energy. Requires Mobile App v4.58.0 or later.

Our brief V14 Lite review with a 2018 Model 3 Performance. A mixed bag, but predominantly positive.

We received V14 Lite yesterday, promptly installed it, and set out on some drives along our usual routes in Torrance, California. Each route we've manually driven and self-driven hundreds of times across every FSD release for both AI3 and AI4.

It is clear that V14 Lite is a leap forward in terms of its capabilities: Its ability to reverse out of parking spots and our garage is incredible and starting a drive with a button press makes end-to-end driving feel great! In one instance, our vehicle reversed to provide additional room for another vehicle who was blocking a crosswalk.

It is clear that Tesla squeezed in a highly performant V14 model. We'd give a rough estimate of ~70-80% the performance of AI4-equipped vehicles based on our own experience and more scientific tests completed by other community members. This is seen via improved response time to cut-ins, faster lane changing, and seemingly better lane positioning during both day and night driving.

With that said; every drive exhibited more hesitation and pausing than on V12.6.4, resulting in an overall less enjoyable experience. All-way stop intersections throughout our city resulted in missed turns due to taking too long to proceed and were honked at twice; something that had not occurred on V12.6.4.

We feel confident that V14 Lite will continue to receive minor revisions and tweaks in the following weeks and months (as it already has between 2026.20.5.1, 2026.20.6.10 and 2026.20.6.11).

As with V12.6.4, Tesla continued to adjust the model despite no point releases or fanfare, and we look forward to the same for V14 Lite.

We use Full Self-Driving on a daily basis, so we're looking forward to future refinements to V14 Lite by @Tesla_AI's incredible team.
